    11. Case Study: The Flutter client for the RdvMedecins application

    11.1. The Problem

    The [RdvMedecins] app allows users to schedule appointments at a doctor's office. The [NestJS] course developed it as a HTML application, in which the server generated the pages; the [Vue.js], [Angular], and [React] wrote web clients for it, which generate the MÊMES pages in the browser, based on the JSON data from the server presented in the chapter “The RdvMedecins Server, a Black Box.” Here we describe the [Flutter] client: a mobile application ([Android]), which can also be compiled for the web.

    The client must provide everything the others did:

    • a login screen, protected by a CAPTCHA, with the option to create a patient account;
    • a doctor’s schedule for a given day, with appointment booking (patient selection window) and cancellation;
    • for the administrator, management of doctors and clients (list, add, edit, delete);
    • for the patient, a personal dashboard (showing upcoming appointments, which they can cancel) and account management;
    • two languages: French and English;
    • the same addresses as the web clients ([/agenda?idMedecin=1&jour=...]). On the phone, they are invisible but organize the app; on the web, users can reload them, bookmark them, and navigate the app using the browser’s Back/Forward buttons.

    A mobile app adds its own requirements: a narrow screen (no five-column tables), a keyboard that hides half the screen, a Back button, a password manager, and the absence of a browser to store the token cookie.

    11.2. Installation and Execution

    The JSON server must be installed and running (see the chapter “The RdvMedecins Server: A Black Box”). You do not need the CAPTCHA test mode: you can leave the [CAPTCHA_TEST] field blank in the [.env] file on the server.

    In a console window open to the [rdvmedecins_flutter] folder:

    1
2
    flutter create --platforms=android,web --org fr.stahe --project-name rdvmedecins_flutter .
flutter pub get

    The first command adds the platform-specific folders ([android/], [web/]) to the project, as in the examples; it does not modify any existing files, and the delivered [android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml] file (the one from Example 22) is retained. Then, choose one of the following:

    1
2
3
    flutter run -d emulator-5554
flutter run -d R58N12ABCDE --dart-define=SERVEUR=http://192.168.1.20:8080
flutter run -d chrome
    • The first line launches the application on the [Android] emulator (the [flutter devices] command lists the available devices). The emulator connects to the server at the address [10.0.2.2:8080] (see Example 22);
    • the second line runs the app on a real phone connected via USB (with “USB debugging” enabled in its developer options) or connected via Wi-Fi. The phone and computer must be on the same network; enter the computer’s address on this network ([ipconfig] under [Windows]). The firewall on [Windows] must allow incoming connections on port 8080;
    • the third, on [Chrome], at the address http://localhost:5173: the web development server in [Flutter] forwards /api requests to the server in JSON (file [web_dev_config.yaml]).

    The demo accounts are listed on the login screen (password = login). While the application is running, the [r] key on the console performs a "hot reload" after a code change; [R] restarts it; [q] stops it.

    Logged in as [admin], you arrive at the calendar. The ☰ button opens the menu: the screens accessible to the administrator, and, at the top, who is logged in:

    Select a doctor and a date (the date in a calendar), then click “View Schedule.” The URL changes to [/agenda?idMedecin=1&jour=2026-10-05]. Clicking “Book” opens the booking window; the URL changes to [/agenda?idMedecin=1&jour=2026-10-05&reserver=3]:

    The appointment is saved; “Cancel” prompts for confirmation:

    A doctor arrives directly at SON. Today's schedule:

    11.3.3. The Patient Portal

    A patient ([martin]) accesses “My Account.” In a calendar, they see “Reserved” next to other patients’ time slots and book an appointment for themselves without selecting a specific patient:

    His appointment appears under his name; the “Book” button is no longer available (only one upcoming appointment). In another doctor’s calendar, where his appointment does not appear, a message explains why he cannot book. His account shows the appointment:

    “Manage My Account”: Any changes require the current password; errors are server-related:

    A patient’s menu does not include a “Doctors” entry. On the web, if the patient types the address /doctors themselves, the router displays a 403 error page (see [routeur.dart]).

    ├── config.dart            l'adresse du serveur
    ├── routeur.dart           les écrans, leurs adresses, leurs droits
    ├── formatage.dart         la mise en forme des heures et des jours
    ├── api/                   la couche d'accès à l'API
    ├── i18n/                  les langues
    ├── etat/                  session, messages, cache (ChangeNotifier)
    ├── widgets/               le gabarit et les widgets réutilisables
    └── pages/                 les écrans

    This is the architecture recommended by the [Flutter] guide (“App architecture”), explained more simply:

    • a data layer ([api/]): the only layer that knows the [http] package, the URLs, and the JSON;
    • a state layer ([etat/]): [ChangeNotifier] objects provided to the entire application ([provider]), which the screens monitor;
    • an interface layer ([pages/], [widgets/]): widgets that display the state and transmit user actions.

    # ==========================================================================
# pubspec.yaml—the Flutter client for the application RdvMedecins
# ==========================================================================

name: rdvmedecins_flutter
description: Le client Flutter (Android, web) de l'application de prise de rendez-vous RdvMedecins.
publish_to: none
version: 1.0.0

environment:
  sdk: ^3.12.0

dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter
  flutter_localizations:
    sdk: flutter
  flutter_web_plugins:
    sdk: flutter
  intl: any
  go_router: ^16.2.0
  provider: ^6.1.5
  shared_preferences: ^2.5.3
  http: ^1.5.0
  flutter_svg: ^2.2.1

dev_dependencies:
  flutter_test:
    sdk: flutter
  flutter_lints: ^6.0.0

flutter:
  uses-material-design: true
  assets:
    - assets/i18n/
  fonts:
    - family: RobotoMono
      fonts:
        - asset: assets/polices/RobotoMono-Regular.ttf
        - asset: assets/polices/RobotoMono-Bold.ttf
          weight: 700

    The example libraries, except for [flutter_svg]... which remains: the CAPTCHA is an image (SVG). The only resources are the dictionaries and the monospaced font for the demo accounts.

    # ==========================================================================
# analysis_options.yaml - the rules of the Dart code analyzer
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The analyzer checks the code as you type (VS Code highlights
# errors) and via the `flutter analyze` command. It is based on the rules
# recommended by the Flutter team (package flutter_lints)...
# ==========================================================================

include: package:flutter_lints/flutter.yaml

analyzer:
  language:
     # ... and make them stricter: no implicit conversion of a `dynamic` type
    strict-casts: true
    strict-raw-types: true

linter:
  rules:
     # single quotes everywhere, as in the examples from the course
    prefer_single_quotes: true
     # "final" for a local variable that is never reassigned
    prefer_final_locals: true
     # Excessively long strings are allowed (French text)
    lines_longer_than_80_chars: false

    The parser’s rules, as shown in the examples:

    • line 9: the rules recommended by the [Flutter] team;
    • lines 14–15: stricter type checking: a [dynamic] (those returned by [jsonDecode]) cannot be used as a [String] without explicit conversion ([as String], or filtering by [Dart] 3);
    • lines 20–24: three formatting rules.

    The [flutter analyze] command applies these rules to the entire project; [VS Code] applies them as you type.

    // =========================================================================
// lib/config.dart - Is OÙ the server JSON?
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// This question does not arise for a web application served by the
// server itself: requests are sent to the origin that the page
// (a relative address, /api/...). But a MOBILE application does not
// origin: you must provide it with the full server address.
//    - The Android emulator sees the computer running it at
//      the address 10.0.2.2 (localhost, which, to the emulator, is the emulator itself);
//    - a real phone, connected to the same Wi-Fi network as the computer, must
//      use the computer’s address on that network (192.168.1.20...):
//      you provide it when launching the app:
//          flutter run --dart-define=SERVEUR=http://192.168.1.20:8080 ...
//    - in web development mode (flutter run -d chrome), the Flutter development server
//      Flutter development server forwards /api requests to the JSON server
//      (file web_dev_config.yaml): a relative address is sufficient;
//    - on a computer (Windows, macOS, Linux): localhost.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';

// the value specified by --dart-define=SERVEUR=..., default is '';
// String.fromEnvironment evaluates to COMPILATION: this is a constant
const _serveurImpose = String.fromEnvironment('SERVEUR');

class Config {
   // kIsWeb: true if the application is running in a browser;
   // defaultTargetPlatform: the system (Android, iOS, Windows...)
  static String urlServeur = _serveurImpose.isNotEmpty
      ? _serveurImpose
      : kIsWeb
      ? '' // same origin: relative addresses
      : defaultTargetPlatform == TargetPlatform.android
      ? 'http://10.0.2.2:8080'
      : 'http://localhost:8080';
}

    The server address, depending on the platform (see Example 22):

    • line 24: the value provided at launch by [--dart-define=SERVEUR=...]. [String.fromEnvironment] is evaluated at compile time: the address is embedded in the built application;
    • lines 29–35: otherwise, a relative address on the web (the development server, then the JSON server itself in production, serve the page ET and API), [10.0.2.2] on [Android] (the computer, as seen from the emulator), [localhost] elsewhere. [static]: a class variable, not an object variable; not [final], so that the tests can modify it.

    // =========================================================================
// lib/main.dart - application startup
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// We create, once and for all, the objects shared by the entire
// the application, then we pass them to all screens (provider):
//    - the HTTP client (which manages the token cookie on the phone) and the
//      access layer to the API;
//    - the session (who is logged in?), messages, and data cache;
//    - translations (French, English);
//    - the router, which displays the screen showing the current address.
// Two mechanisms link these objects together:
//    1. the 401 response to a protected request (session expired): the user is logged out
//       the user and prepare the message; the router, which is listening for the
//       session, then redirects to the login screen (see api/client_api.dart);
//    2. “Flash” messages: at the end of CHAQUE navigation, the messages
//       from the previous screen disappear, and the following messages
//       appear (see status/messages.dart).
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter_localizations/flutter_localizations.dart';
import 'package:flutter_web_plugins/url_strategy.dart';
import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';
import 'package:intl/date_symbol_data_local.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';

import 'api/client_api.dart';
import 'api/client_http.dart';
import 'api/rdvmedecins_api.dart';
import 'etat/cache.dart';
import 'etat/messages.dart';
import 'etat/session.dart';
import 'i18n/traductions.dart';
import 'routeur.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();
  usePathUrlStrategy(); // on the web: /agenda rather than /#/agenda
  await initializeDateFormatting();
  final stockage = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
  final traductions = Traductions(stockage);
  await traductions.demarrer();
  runApp(Application(stockage: stockage, traductions: traductions));
}

class Application extends StatefulWidget {
  final SharedPreferences stockage;
  final Traductions traductions;

  const Application({super.key, required this.stockage, required this.traductions});

  @override
  State<Application> createState() => _ApplicationState();
}

class _ApplicationState extends State<Application> {
  late final ClientApi _client = ClientApi(ClientAvecCookies(widget.stockage));
  late final RdvMedecinsApi _api = RdvMedecinsApi(_client);
  late final Session _session = Session(_api);
  final Messages _messages = Messages();
  final Cache _cache = Cache();
  late final GoRouter _routeur = creerRouteur(_session, _messages, _api);
  String? _adresse;

  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
     // 1. Session expired
    _client.onSessionExpiree = () {
      _session.oublier();
      _cache.vider();
      _messages.flash(succes: false, cle: 'ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED');
       // no _routeur.go('/login'): the router handles this, and
       // saves the current screen (?redirect=...) to return to it
    };
     // the session changes (login, logout): the data read for
     // the previous user is no longer valid
    _session.addListener(_cache.vider);
     // 2. After each navigation is complete (the address has changed): new page
    _routeur.routerDelegate.addListener(() {
       // state: the DESSUS screen on the stack (including one screen pushed onto the stack)
      final adresse = _routeur.state.uri.toString();
      if (adresse != _adresse) {
        _adresse = adresse;
        _messages.nouvellePage();
      }
    });
  }

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _routeur.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return MultiProvider(
      providers: [
         // ordinary objects...
        Provider.value(value: _api),
         // ... and objects that notify of their changes
        ChangeNotifierProvider.value(value: _cache),
        ChangeNotifierProvider.value(value: _session),
        ChangeNotifierProvider.value(value: _messages),
        ChangeNotifierProvider.value(value: widget.traductions),
      ],
      child: Consumer<Traductions>(
        builder: (context, traductions, _) => MaterialApp.router(
          debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
          onGenerateTitle: (context) => traductions.t('APP.TITLE'),
          theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: const Color(0xFF0D6EFD)),
           // Flutter’s own text (calendar...) in the selected language
          locale: Locale(traductions.langue),
          supportedLocales: [for (final l in langues) Locale(l)],
          localizationsDelegates: GlobalMaterialLocalizations.delegates,
          routerConfig: _routeur,
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
    • lines 37–44: Before displaying anything, we prepare what needs to be prepared: web addresses without [#] (example 17), the names of days and months in all languages ([intl], example 09), the device’s storage, and the source language dictionary. [WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()]: These operations require the [Flutter] engine, so we start it before [runApp];
    • lines 58–63: the shared objects, created UNE times, in the root widget’s state. Each receives the ones it needs upon creation: this is dependency injection, done manually. [late]: Initialization occurs upon first use, when [widget] already exists;
    • lines 70–76: 1. the expired session. The access layer for API is unaware of either the session or the messages; it is entrusted with this function, which it will call upon every 401 response. The user is forgotten, the cache is cleared, and the message for the next screen is prepared. The screen transition itself is handled by the router, which monitors the session;
    • line 79: every time the user changes, the cache is cleared: the data read for the previous user is of no use to the next one (a patient should not see the calendar viewed by the administrator);
    • Lines 81–88: 2. Flash messages. The router’s [routerDelegate] alerts its listeners with each transmission; the address is compared to the previous one ([_routeur.state]: the screen state of the stack’s DESSUS, including a screen stacked by [push], such as the reservation window), and, if it has changed, the system moves to a “new page”: the messages from the previous screen disappear, and those placed on this one appear (see [messages.dart]);
    • lines 99–107: shared objects are provided to all screens (Example 20). [.value]: the object already exists; the provider does not create it (and will not destroy it);
    • lines 109–118: the application itself, rebuilt with every language change ([Consumer], see Example 20): the title ([onGenerateTitle]), and the language of the text in [Flutter] itself (the calendar, tooltips). [colorSchemeSeed]: a color from which [Material] derives the entire palette; this is the blue of [Bootstrap], the color used by web clients.

    // =========================================================================
// lib/api/client_http.dart - a HTTP client that handles COOKIES
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The RdvMedecins server places the JWT token in a COOKIE (httpOnly).
// In a browser, it is the browser that stores cookies and
// sends them back with every request: the application code has nothing to do with it.
// On a phone, there is no PAS browser: it’s up to the app to
// take on that role, which means:
//    1. read the "Set-Cookie" header in each response and store the cookies;
//    2. send them back in the “Cookie” header of each request.
// This client (HTTP) does this; in ENVELOPPANT, the client in the HTTP package
// (http.BaseClient: simply call the `send` method). The cookies are
// also stored on the device (shared_preferences): you remain logged in
// even when you close and then reopen the app.
// On the web, it does nothing more than a regular client: the
// browser prevents the app from reading or writing these headers.
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';
import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';

class ClientAvecCookies extends http.BaseClient {
  static const _cle = 'rdvmedecins.cookies';

  final http.Client _interne = http.Client();
  final SharedPreferences? _stockage;
   // cookie name -> its value
  final Map<String, String> _cookies = {};

  ClientAvecCookies([this._stockage]) {
     // cookies stored from a previous session
    final memorises = _stockage?.getString(_cle);
    if (memorises != null) {
      _cookies.addAll((jsonDecode(memorises) as Map<String, Object?>).cast<String, String>());
    }
  }

  @override
  Future<http.StreamedResponse> send(http.BaseRequest requete) async {
    if (!kIsWeb && _cookies.isNotEmpty) {
       // "rdvmedecins_jwt=eyJhbGci...; other=value"
      requete.headers['cookie'] = [for (final MapEntry(:key, :value) in _cookies.entries) '$key=$value'].join('; ');
    }
    final reponse = await _interne.send(requete);
    final setCookie = reponse.headers['set-cookie'];
    if (!kIsWeb && setCookie != null) {
      _memoriser(setCookie);
    }
    return reponse;
  }

   // Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=eyJ...; Max-Age=7200; Path=/api; Expires=Tue, Sep 29, 2026 ...; HttpOnly
   // (multiple cookies are separated by commas). We only keep the
   // name and value of each cookie; an empty value (logout) deletes it
  void _memoriser(String setCookie) {
     // a name followed by "=", at the beginning of the header or after a comma
    for (final m in RegExp(r'(?:^|,)\s*([^=;,\s]+)=([^;]*)').allMatches(setCookie)) {
      final nom = m[1]!;
      final valeur = m[2]!.trim();
      if (valeur.isEmpty) {
        _cookies.remove(nom);
      } else {
        _cookies[nom] = valeur;
      }
    }
    _stockage?.setString(_cle, jsonEncode(_cookies));
  }

  @override
  void close() => _interne.close();
}

    The HTTP client from Example 23, unchanged: it stores the received cookies ([Set-Cookie] header) and sends them back ([Cookie] header) to the phone; on the web, it lets the browser handle it.

    // =========================================================================
// lib/api/client_api.dart - TOUTES requests to API go through here
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Taken from the examples in commun/api.dart, with a new feature: centralized handling
// centralized handling of the 401 response.
//
// A 401 can occur at any time: the token has expired (2 hours), the
// account has been deleted, or the server has restarted with a different key
// is hidden... Rather than handling this case on every screen, it is handled
// ICI, just once. But this file knows neither the router nor the messages
// (it is independent of anything else): it calls a function that was assigned to it at
// startup (onSessionExpiree, see main.dart), which ignores the user and
// redirects to the login page.
//
// Some requests handle their own 401 responses (login, GET
// /api/auth/me...): these are "public" (see rdvmedecins_api.dart).
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;

import '../config.dart';
import 'erreur_api.dart';

class ClientApi {
  final http.Client _client;
   // What to do when the server returns a 401 response to a protected request
  void Function() onSessionExpiree = () {};

  ClientApi(this._client);

   // public: true for routes that handle the 401 themselves
  Future<Object?> requete(String methode, String url, {Object? corps, bool publique = false}) async {
    final requete = http.Request(methode, Uri.parse('${Config.urlServeur}/api$url'));
    if (corps != null) {
      requete.headers['content-type'] = 'application/json';
      requete.body = jsonEncode(corps);
    }
    final http.Response reponse;
    try {
      reponse = await http.Response.fromStream(await _client.send(requete));
    } catch (_) {
       // No response: network down, server stopped, incorrect address
      throw const ErreurApi(0, 'ERRORS.SERVER_UNREACHABLE');
    }
    if (reponse.statusCode >= 400) {
      final erreur = ErreurApi.depuisReponse(reponse);
      if (erreur.statusCode == 401 && !publique) {
        onSessionExpiree();
         // The screen that was waiting for the response will also display the CE message
        throw const ErreurApi(401, 'ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED');
      }
      throw erreur;
    }
    return reponse.bodyBytes.isEmpty ? null : jsonDecode(utf8.decode(reponse.bodyBytes));
  }
}

    The [commun/api.dart] file from the examples, with a new feature: the 401 response.

    • Line 29: a function to call in the event of a 401 error, specified at startup (see [main.dart]). By default, it does nothing;
    • line 34: [publique] is a named, optional parameter (enclosed in curly braces): [requete('GET', '/captcha', publique: true)];
    • lines 35–38: the request, built piece by piece: method, address, header, and body JSON;
    • lines 40–45: the request is sent. An exception here means that no response was received (network down, server down, incorrect address). [final http.Response reponse;]: a variable [final] declared without a value; [Dart] checks that it receives a value—only once—before being read;
    • lines 47–54: an error response becomes a [ErreurApi]. A 401 on a protected request means the session has expired: [onSessionExpiree] is called, then an error is triggered anyway (the screen that was waiting for the response must know that it did not arrive), using the key [ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED]: if this screen displays the error, it is the same message;
    • line 56: a response with no body (204) yields [null]. We decode the bytes to UTF-8: without the header [charset], the packet [http] would decode to [reponse.body] in Latin-1, and the accents would be corrupted.

    // =========================================================================
// lib/api/erreur_api.dart - UNE class for all API errors
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// All error responses from the RdvMedecins server have the same format:
//    { "statusCode": 409, "key": "ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN", "params": {...}, "fields": {...} }
// But a request can also fail (AUTREMENT): no response at all
// (network down, server down, incorrect address), or a response that
// doesn’t come from our server (an error page from a proxy). We convert
// all of this into the UNE class, ErreurApi, which carries the translation key
// sent by the server (and, if any, its parameters and the error for
// for each field).
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;

// "implements Exception": an object that can be thrown and caught
class ErreurApi implements Exception {
  final int statusCode; // 0: the server did not respond
  final String cle; // e.g., 'ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN'
  final Map<String, String> params;
  final Map<String, String> champs;

  const ErreurApi(this.statusCode, this.cle, {this.params = const {}, this.champs = const {}});

   // an error response (4xx, 5xx) -> a ErreurApi
  factory ErreurApi.depuisReponse(http.Response reponse) {
    Object? corps;
    try {
      corps = jsonDecode(utf8.decode(reponse.bodyBytes));
    } on FormatException {
      corps = null; // not JSON: this response did not come from our server
    }
     // "filtering" (pattern matching) of a Map: if the body has a key
     // "key" of type String, it is stored in the variable key
    if (corps case {'cle': final String cle}) {
      final json = corps as Map<String, Object?>;
      return ErreurApi(reponse.statusCode, cle, params: _chaines(json['params']), champs: _chaines(json['champs']));
    }
     // No key: the proxy or the network responded instead
    return ErreurApi(
      reponse.statusCode,
      reponse.statusCode >= 500 ? 'ERRORS.SERVER_UNREACHABLE' : 'ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR',
    );
  }

   // an object JSON { "name": "ERRORS..." } -> Map<String, String> (empty otherwise)
  static Map<String, String> _chaines(Object? json) =>
      json is Map<String, Object?> ? {for (final e in json.entries) e.key: '${e.value}'} : const {};

  @override
  String toString() => '$statusCode $cle';
}

    The one from Example 24: any request that fails ends with a [ErreurApi], which contains the message’s translation key, its parameters, and the error for each field.

    // =========================================================================
// lib/api/types.dart - JSON objects exchanged with the server
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The translation, into Dart classes, of the API described in the chapter "The
// server, a black box" (see the examples in `commun/types.dart`). Each
// class processes its JSON using Dart 3 filtering: a response that does not
// the expected format is detected as soon as it is received.
// =========================================================================

enum Role { admin, doctor, user }

Role _role(String nom) => Role.values.byName(nom.toLowerCase());

Never _inattendu(String quoi, Object? json) => throw FormatException('$quoi inattendu : $json');

// POST /api/auth/login, GET /api/auth/me, PUT /api/my-account
class Utilisateur {
  final String login;
  final String nom; // display name: "Marie PELISSIER"
  final Role role;

  const Utilisateur(this.login, this.nom, this.role);

  factory Utilisateur.depuisJson(Object? json) => switch (json) {
    {'login': final String login, 'nom': final String nom, 'role': final String role} => Utilisateur(
      login,
      nom,
      _role(role),
    ),
    _ => _inattendu('Utilisateur', json),
  };
}

// GET /api/captcha
class Captcha {
  final String id;
  final String svg;

  const Captcha(this.id, this.svg);

  factory Captcha.depuisJson(Object? json) => switch (json) {
    {'id': final String id, 'svg': final String svg} => Captcha(id, svg),
    _ => _inattendu('Captcha', json),
  };
}

// a title, a first name, a last name
class Identite {
  final String titre;
  final String prenom;
  final String nom;

  const Identite(this.titre, this.prenom, this.nom);

  factory Identite.depuisJson(Object? json) => switch (json) {
    {'titre': final String titre, 'prenom': final String prenom, 'nom': final String nom} => Identite(
      titre,
      prenom,
      nom,
    ),
    _ => _inattendu('Identité', json),
  };

   // "Ms. Alice DURAND"
  String get libelle => '$titre $prenom $nom';
}

// a doctor or a client: GET /api/doctors, GET /api/clients/:id...
class Personne extends Identite {
  final int id;
  final int version; // optimistic lock: to be sent back with a modification
  final String? login; // only for ADMIN

  const Personne(this.id, this.version, super.titre, super.prenom, super.nom, [this.login]);

  factory Personne.depuisJson(Object? json) => switch (json) {
    {
      'id': final int id,
      'version': final int version,
      'titre': final String titre,
      'prenom': final String prenom,
      'nom': final String nom,
    } =>
      Personne(id, version, titre, prenom, nom, (json as Map<String, Object?>)['login'] as String?),
    _ => _inattendu('Personne', json),
  };

  static List<Personne> liste(Object? json) => [for (final p in json as List<Object?>) Personne.depuisJson(p)];
}

// a time slot
class Creneau {
  final int id;
  final int hdebut;
  final int mdebut;
  final int hfin;
  final int mfin;

  const Creneau(this.id, this.hdebut, this.mdebut, this.hfin, this.mfin);

  factory Creneau.depuisJson(Object? json) => switch (json) {
    {'id': final int id, 'hdebut': final int hd, 'mdebut': final int md, 'hfin': final int hf, 'mfin': final int mf} =>
      Creneau(id, hd, md, hf, mf),
    _ => _inattendu('Créneau', json),
  };
}

// a calendar entry, with the DROITS of the logged-in user
class CreneauAgenda extends Creneau {
  final bool libre;
  final Identite? patient; // null: available, or booked by another patient
  final bool moi; // the logged-in patient’s appointment
  final bool reservable;
  final int? idRv; // specified if the user can cancel

  const CreneauAgenda(
    super.id,
    super.hdebut,
    super.mdebut,
    super.hfin,
    super.mfin,
    this.libre,
    this.patient,
    this.moi,
    this.reservable,
    this.idRv,
  );

  factory CreneauAgenda.depuisJson(Object? json) {
    final c = Creneau.depuisJson(json);
    return switch (json) {
      {
        'libre': final bool libre,
        'patient': final Object? patient,
        'moi': final bool moi,
        'reservable': final bool reservable,
        'idRv': final int? idRv,
      } =>
        CreneauAgenda(
          c.id,
          c.hdebut,
          c.mdebut,
          c.hfin,
          c.mfin,
          libre,
          patient == null ? null : Identite.depuisJson(patient),
          moi,
          reservable,
          idRv,
        ),
      _ => _inattendu('Créneau', json),
    };
  }
}

// GET /api/agenda?idMedecin=...&day=...
class Agenda {
  final Personne medecin;
  final String jour; // "yyyy-MM-dd"
  final List<CreneauAgenda> creneaux;
  final String? info; // translation key (patient who already has an appointment)

  const Agenda(this.medecin, this.jour, this.creneaux, this.info);

  factory Agenda.depuisJson(Object? json) => switch (json) {
    {
      'medecin': final Object medecin,
      'jour': final String jour,
      'creneaux': final List<Object?> creneaux,
      'info': final String? info,
    } =>
      Agenda(Personne.depuisJson(medecin), jour, [for (final c in creneaux) CreneauAgenda.depuisJson(c)], info),
    _ => _inattendu('Agenda', json),
  };
}

// an appointment from GET /api/my-space
class RendezVous {
  final int id;
  final String jour;
  final Creneau creneau;
  final Personne medecin;

  const RendezVous(this.id, this.jour, this.creneau, this.medecin);

  factory RendezVous.depuisJson(Object? json) => switch (json) {
    {'id': final int id, 'jour': final String jour, 'creneau': final Object creneau, 'medecin': final Object medecin} =>
      RendezVous(id, jour, Creneau.depuisJson(creneau), Personne.depuisJson(medecin)),
    _ => _inattendu('Rendez-vous', json),
  };
}

// GET /api/my-space
class MonEspace {
  final Identite patient;
  final List<RendezVous> rendezVous;

  const MonEspace(this.patient, this.rendezVous);

  factory MonEspace.depuisJson(Object? json) => switch (json) {
    {'patient': final Object patient, 'rendezVous': final List<Object?> rv} => MonEspace(Identite.depuisJson(patient), [
      for (final r in rv) RendezVous.depuisJson(r),
    ]),
    _ => _inattendu('Espace', json),
  };
}

// GET /api/my-account
class MonCompte extends Identite {
  final String login;
  final int version;

  const MonCompte(super.titre, super.prenom, super.nom, this.login, this.version);

  factory MonCompte.depuisJson(Object? json) {
    final i = Identite.depuisJson(json);
    return switch (json) {
      {'login': final String login, 'version': final int version} => MonCompte(
        i.titre,
        i.prenom,
        i.nom,
        login,
        version,
      ),
      _ => _inattendu('Compte', json),
    };
  }
}

    The JSON objects from API, in [Dart] classes (see Example 24):

    • line 14: a function that never terminates normally (it throws an exception): its return type is [Never]. It can therefore serve as the final case for a [switch] of any type;
    • lines 24–30: filtering a [Map]: this case applies if the JSON has (at least) these three keys, with values of these types, which are stored in variables along the way;
    • lines 69–88: a doctor or a client: a [Identite], plus an identifier, a version (the optimistic lock: it will be released upon a modification), and a login, which only the ADMIN receives (hence the optional parameter in square brackets);
    • Lines 109–114: An entry in the calendar, showing the DROITS for the logged-in user, calculated by the server: [patient] is only shown to those who have permission to view it, [reservable] indicates whether the user can make a reservation; [idRv] is only provided to those who can cancel;
    • lines 129–151: first, the time slot itself ([Creneau.depuisJson]) is read, followed by its specific fields;
    • lines 209–213: the logged-in patient’s account: their identity, login, and version. [super.titre]: the parameter is passed as-is to the parent class constructor.

    // =========================================================================
// lib/api/rdvmedecins_api.dart - a method per route from API
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The client’s “data access layer” (a “repository,” in the
// terminology of the Flutter architecture guide): the screens call
// these typed methods without knowing anything about URL, the http package, or the
// JSON. If the API changes, only this file changes.
// Each method returns a Future; if it fails, it ends with a
// ErreurApi (see client_api.dart).
// The data sent (forms) are simple Map<String, Object>?> :
// Their keys are the names of the fields expected by the server—and those
// of the errors it returns (ErreurApi.champs).
// =========================================================================

import 'client_api.dart';
import 'types.dart';

// /api/doctors or /api/clients: both are handled the same way
enum TypePersonnes { medecins, clients }

typedef Donnees = Map<String, Object?>;

class RdvMedecinsApi {
  final ClientApi _client;

  RdvMedecinsApi(this._client);

  Future<Object?> _get(String url, {bool publique = false}) => _client.requete('GET', url, publique: publique);
  Future<Object?> _post(String url, Object corps, {bool publique = false}) =>
      _client.requete('POST', url, corps: corps, publique: publique);

   // ------------------------------------------------ login (public routes)
  Future<Captcha> captcha() async => Captcha.depuisJson(await _get('/captcha', publique: true));

  Future<Utilisateur> moi() async => Utilisateur.depuisJson(await _get('/auth/moi', publique: true));

  Future<Utilisateur> connecter(String login, String password, String captchaId, String captcha) async =>
      Utilisateur.depuisJson(
        await _post('/auth/login', {
          'login': login,
          'password': password,
          'captchaId': captchaId,
          'captcha': captcha,
        }, publique: true),
      );

  Future<void> deconnecter() => _post('/auth/logout', {}, publique: true);

   // ------------------------------------------------ account creation (public)
  Future<void> accesInscription(String captchaId, String captcha) =>
      _post('/inscription/acces', {'captchaId': captchaId, 'captcha': captcha}, publique: true);

  Future<bool> etatAccesInscription() async => switch (await _get('/inscription/acces', publique: true)) {
    {'valide': true} => true,
    _ => false,
  };

  Future<String> inscrire(Donnees donnees) async => switch (await _post('/inscription', donnees, publique: true)) {
    {'login': final String login} => login,
    final autre => throw FormatException('Réponse inattendue : $autre'),
  };

   // ------------------------------------------------ calendar and appointments
   // idMedecin null: for a logged-in doctor, SON calendar
  Future<Agenda> agenda(int? idMedecin, String jour) async {
    final parametres = Uri(queryParameters: {'jour': jour, 'idMedecin': ?idMedecin?.toString()}).query;
    return Agenda.depuisJson(await _get('/agenda?$parametres'));
  }

  Future<void> reserver(String jour, int idCreneau, int? idClient) =>
      _post('/rendez-vous', {'jour': jour, 'idCreneau': idCreneau, 'idClient': ?idClient});

  Future<void> annulerRv(int idRv) => _client.requete('DELETE', '/rendez-vous/$idRv');

   // ------------------------------------------------ doctors and clients
  Future<List<Personne>> lister(TypePersonnes type) async => Personne.liste(await _get('/${type.name}'));

  Future<Personne> lire(TypePersonnes type, int id) async => Personne.depuisJson(await _get('/${type.name}/$id'));

  Future<Personne> ajouter(TypePersonnes type, Donnees donnees) async =>
      Personne.depuisJson(await _post('/${type.name}', donnees));

  Future<Personne> modifier(TypePersonnes type, int id, Donnees donnees) async =>
      Personne.depuisJson(await _client.requete('PUT', '/${type.name}/$id', corps: donnees));

  Future<void> supprimer(TypePersonnes type, int id) => _client.requete('DELETE', '/${type.name}/$id');

   // ------------------------------------------------ Patient Area
  Future<MonEspace> monEspace() async => MonEspace.depuisJson(await _get('/mon-espace'));

  Future<MonCompte> monCompte() async => MonCompte.depuisJson(await _get('/mon-compte'));

  Future<Utilisateur> modifierMonCompte(Donnees donnees) async =>
      Utilisateur.depuisJson(await _client.requete('PUT', '/mon-compte', corps: donnees));

  Future<void> supprimerMonCompte(String motDePasseActuel) =>
      _client.requete('DELETE', '/mon-compte', corps: {'motDePasseActuel': motDePasseActuel});
}

    A method per route for API: this is the [RdvMedecins] class from Example 24, expanded.

    • Line 19: [/api/medecins] and [/api/clients] are handled the same way: an enumeration, where the name of each value ([TypePersonnes.medecins.name], “doctors”) is that of the route;
    • Line 21: A type alias: a more descriptive name for an existing type;
    • lines 33–47: the connection routes, which are public: a 401 has its own specific meaning (“no one is logged in,” “incorrect password”) and does not mean that the session has expired;
    • line 53: Is the account creation token valid? A [switch] expression in the response: [true] only for [{"valide": true}];
    • Lines 65–67: The address parameters, constructed by [Uri] (which encodes them). ['idMedecin': ?idMedecin?.toString()]: an optional element of [Map] ([Dart] 3.8): the key is added only if the value is not [null]. A logged-in doctor requests the calendar without [idMedecin]: the server returns the doctor’s own calendar;
    • line 71: similarly, [idClient] is sent only if it is known (a patient is making a reservation for themselves);
    • lines 76–86: the five operations involving doctors or clients: [/api/${type.name}];
    • lines 89–97: the patient’s space. Deleting the account sends a message body with a [DELETE] request (the current password): this is permitted by HTTP, and the [http] package also allows it, via a manually constructed [http.Request] (see [client_api.dart]).

    // =========================================================================
// lib/i18n/traductions.dart - dictionaries, current language
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Taken from Example 21. The dictionaries (assets/i18n/fr.json, en.json)
// are those for the Vue.js, Angular, and React clients: same keys, same
// conventions ({{param}}, plurals _one / _other). The server does not return
// only CLÉS ("ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN"): this is where they become
// text in the language selected by the user.
//    - t('CLE', {'param': value}) : the text in the current language;
//    - changerLangue('en'        ) : loads the other dictionary, notifies
//                                    the screens (ChangeNotifier), saves
//                                    the selection on the device.
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:flutter/services.dart';
import 'package:flutter/widgets.dart';
import 'package:intl/intl.dart';
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';

const langues = ['fr', 'en'];

class Traductions extends ChangeNotifier {
  final SharedPreferences? _stockage;
  String _langue = 'fr';
  Map<String, Object?> _dictionnaire = {};

  Traductions([this._stockage]);

  String get langue => _langue;

   // the source language: the one stored on the device, otherwise the language of the
   // phone (if known), otherwise French
  Future<void> demarrer() async {
    final memorisee = _stockage?.getString('rdvmedecins.langue');
    final appareil = WidgetsBinding.instance.platformDispatcher.locale.languageCode;
    await changerLangue(memorisee ?? (langues.contains(appareil) ? appareil : 'fr'));
  }

  Future<void> changerLangue(String langue) async {
     // rootBundle: the files included with the application (the "assets" section of the pubspec)
    final json = await rootBundle.loadString('assets/i18n/$langue.json');
    _dictionnaire = jsonDecode(json) as Map<String, Object?>;
    _langue = langue;
    await _stockage?.setString('rdvmedecins.langue', langue);
    notifyListeners();
  }

   // "ACCUEIL.BONJOUR" -> dictionaryQZXW2HTMLBWydBQ0NVRUlMJ10ZQXQZXW2HTMLBWydCT05KT1VSJ10ZQX; null if absent
  String? _chercher(String cle) {
    Object? noeud = _dictionnaire;
    for (final partie in cle.split('.')) {
      noeud = noeud is Map<String, Object?> ? noeud[partie] : null;
    }
    return noeud is String ? noeud : null;
  }

  String t(String cle, [Map<String, Object?> params = const {}]) {
    String? texte;
    final count = params['count'];
    if (count is int) {
       // Intl.pluralLogic: the plural form, according to the rules of the language
      texte = Intl.pluralLogic(
        count,
        locale: _langue,
        zero: _chercher('${cle}_zero'),
        one: _chercher('${cle}_one'),
        other: _chercher('${cle}_other'),
      );
    }
    texte ??= _chercher(cle);
     // an unknown key is displayed as-is: you can immediately see what’s missing
    if (texte == null) return cle;
     // {{name}} -> the value of the “name” parameter
    return texte.replaceAllMapped(RegExp(r'\{\{(\w+)\}\}'), (m) => '${params[m[1]] ?? m[0]}');
  }
}

    The [Traductions] class from Example 21, simplified: the dictionaries always have the same name ([assets/i18n/fr.json]).

    • lines 35–38: the source language: the one selected during a previous use, otherwise the phone’s language if the app knows it, otherwise French. [platformDispatcher.locale]: the system language;
    • lines 59–76: the translation of a key, including plurals ([_zero], [_one], [_other]) and parameters ([{{nom}}]), according to the conventions of [i18next], which are the same as those used in the dictionaries of other clients.

    // =========================================================================
// lib/etat/session.dart - Is QUI logged in?
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The logged-in user (or null), in a ChangeNotifier provided to any
// application (provider, see Example 20): readable by the ET screens via
// the router, which listens for it to reevaluate its guards (refreshListenable).
//
// The JWT token itself is not present here: it is stored in a cookie (managed by the
// web browser, or by ClientAvecCookies on the phone). The
// session only stores the user’s DESCRIPTION ({ login, name, role }).
//
// When the application starts, the session is empty: `verifier()` sends
// the server—only once—to check which user is logged in (GET /api/auth/moi).
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';

import '../api/rdvmedecins_api.dart';
import '../api/types.dart';

class Session extends ChangeNotifier {
  final RdvMedecinsApi _api;
  Utilisateur? _utilisateur;
   // true after a logout (VOULUE; button, account deletion); false
   // after a session has expired. The router takes this into account (see routeur.dart)
  bool _departVolontaire = false;
   // Has the question “Who is logged in?” already been asked of the server?
  Future<void>? _verification;

  Session(this._api);

  Utilisateur? get utilisateur => _utilisateur;
  bool get departVolontaire => _departVolontaire;

   // only queries the server the first time (the Future is retained)
  Future<void> verifier() => _verification ??= _api.moi().then(
    (u) => _changer(u),
    onError: (Object _) => _changer(null), // 401: No one; or server unreachable
  );

  Future<void> connecter(String login, String password, String captchaId, String captcha) async {
    _changer(await _api.connecter(login, password, captchaId, captcha));
  }

   // The user has changed their name or login (PUT /api/my-account)
  void mettreAJour(Utilisateur u) => _changer(u);

  Future<void> deconnecter() async {
    try {
      await _api.deconnecter();
    } finally {
      oublier(volontaire: true);
    }
  }

   // without making a request to the server: session expired, account deleted
  void oublier({bool volontaire = false}) => _changer(null, volontaire: volontaire);

   // notifyListeners: the router (refreshListenable) reevaluates its guards, and
   // automatically exits a screen that the new user is not authorized to view
  void _changer(Utilisateur? u, {bool volontaire = false}) {
    _utilisateur = u;
    _departVolontaire = volontaire;
    notifyListeners();
  }
}

// which we infer from the user: extensions (getter methods added to User?)
extension Droits on Utilisateur? {
  bool get estAdmin => this?.role == Role.admin;
  bool get estPatient => this?.role == Role.user;
   // ADMIN and DOCTOR: schedule and cancel appointments for any patient
  bool get estGestionnaire => this?.role == Role.admin || this?.role == Role.doctor;
   // the home page for each role, immediately after logging in
  String get pageAccueil => estPatient ? '/mon-espace' : '/agenda';
}

    Who is logged in? The session stores the user's DESCRIPTION (login, name, role), not the token, which remains in the user's cookie.

    • Lines 36–38: The question “Who is logged in?” is sent to the server ([GET /api/auth/moi]) UNE only once, at startup: [??=] only affects [Future] if [_verification] is [null]. Subsequent calls return the same [Future], which has already been completed: the router can call [verifier()] before each navigation at no cost. At startup, if the stored cookie contains a token that is still valid, the user remains logged in;
    • lines 41–42: the connection: if the server refuses, [_api.connecter] initiates a [ErreurApi], and [_changer] is not called;
    • lines 48–52: logout: the user is forgotten even if the server does not respond ([finally]);
    • lines 61–64: all changes go through here, and notify the listeners: the screens displaying the user (the template), the cache (which is cleared), and the router (which reevaluates its guards). [_departVolontaire] distinguishes between an intentional logout and an expired session (see [routeur.dart]);
    • lines 69–75: an extension adds getters to an existing type, in this case [Utilisateur?]: [session.utilisateur.estAdmin] is [false] if no one is logged in, without first checking for [null] ([this?.role]).

    // =========================================================================
// lib/etat/messages.dart - messages displayed to the user
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Same layout as other clients of RdvMedecins:
//    - a SUCCÈS is displayed as HAUT on the screen (green banner);
//    - a ERREUR appears as BAS (pink banner), which remains visible.
// A message is a translation CLÉ (+ its settings): it is therefore re-translated
// on its own if the user changes the language.
//
// "Flash" messages: an action that ends with a change
// (reservation, adding a doctor, etc.) places its message with
// flash(); it will appear on the SUIVANT screen, then disappear upon
// next page transition. The router calls nouvellePage() at the
// end of each navigation (see routeur.dart).
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';

import '../api/erreur_api.dart';

typedef Message = ({String cle, Map<String, String> params});

class Messages extends ChangeNotifier {
  Message? succes;
  Message? erreur;
   // the messages to display on the next screen
  Message? _succesEnAttente;
  Message? _erreurEnAttente;

  void afficherSucces(String cle, [Map<String, String> params = const {}]) {
    succes = (cle: cle, params: params);
    erreur = null;
    notifyListeners();
  }

  void afficherErreur(String cle, [Map<String, String> params = const {}]) {
    erreur = (cle: cle, params: params);
    succes = null;
    notifyListeners();
  }

   // a ErreurApi -> the screen message; any other error is a
   // client error, which is allowed to be reported
  void afficherErreurApi(Object e) {
    if (e is! ErreurApi) throw e;
    afficherErreur(e.cle, e.params);
  }

  void effacer() {
    succes = null;
    erreur = null;
    notifyListeners();
  }

   // for screen SUIVANT
  void flash({bool succes = true, required String cle, Map<String, String> params = const {}}) {
    if (succes) {
      _succesEnAttente = (cle: cle, params: params);
    } else {
      _erreurEnAttente = (cle: cle, params: params);
    }
  }

   // a new screen: the messages from the previous screen disappear, and the
   // flash messages appear
  void nouvellePage() {
    succes = _succesEnAttente;
    erreur = _erreurEnAttente;
    _succesEnAttente = null;
    _erreurEnAttente = null;
    notifyListeners();
  }
}

    Application messages: a success message at the top of the screen, an error message at the bottom (see [gabarit.dart]).

    • Line 21: A message is a CLÉ translation record and its parameters (a single record). It is translated only when displayed: changing the language re-translates the displayed messages;
    • Lines 44–46: A [ErreurApi] becomes the screen’s error message. Any other exception is a client-side issue: we re-throw it so that it appears in the console during development, rather than hiding it;
    • lines 56–60: a message for screen SUIVANT: an action that ends with a screen change (a reservation, an addition, etc.) places its message here;
    • lines 66–71: called every time the address changes (see [main.dart]): messages from the previous screen disappear, and flash messages appear.

    // =========================================================================
// lib/etat/cache.dart—the data already read from the server
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The list of doctors hardly ever changes: no need to reload it
// every time you visit the calendar. The cache stores the Future of each read,
// under a CLÉ ('doctors', 'calendar/1/2026-10-05'...):
//
//      cache.lire('doctors', () => api.lister(TypePersonnes.medecins))
//
// returns the Future that has already been cached, or initiates the read operation and caches it.
// After a modification, the affected keys are INVALIDE (they will be
// read again on the next request): cache.invalider('agenda').
// A failed read is not retained: the next request will retry.
// The cache is a ChangeNotifier: invalidate() notifies its listeners. A
// screen is still active (even if hidden under another one in the stack, such as
// the calendar beneath its booking window) can thus read its data again.
// In a nutshell, this is what the TanStack Query library of the
// React client.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';

class Cache extends ChangeNotifier {
  final Map<String, Future<Object?>> _futurs = {};

  Future<T> lire<T>(String cle, Future<T> Function() charger) {
    final futur = _futurs.putIfAbsent(cle, () {
      final f = charger();
       // If the request fails, this Future is discarded (the next request will retry)
      f.then((_) {}, onError: (Object _) => _futurs.remove(cle));
      return f;
    });
    return futur.then((v) => v as T);
  }

   // Discards all keys that start with the prefix and notifies the screens
  void invalider(String prefixe) {
    _futurs.removeWhere((cle, _) => cle.startsWith(prefixe));
    notifyListeners();
  }

   // user switch: everything is discarded; SANS notifies (the screens from
   // the previous user will disappear; they must not re-read anything)
  void vider() => _futurs.clear();
}

    Data already read from the server: the equivalent, in a few lines, of [TanStack Query] in the [React] client.

    • Line 24: The cache stores [Future], not actual values: two screens requesting the same data while it is in transit receive MÊME and [Future], and only a single request is sent;
    • Lines 26–33: A generic method: [lire<List<Personne>>(...)] returns a [Future<List<Personne>>] (the type [T] is most often inferred from the function [charger]). [putIfAbsent]: the value of the key, or, if the key is missing, the result of the function, stored under that key. A failed read is ignored: the next request will try again;
    • lines 37–39: After a modification, the affected keys are discarded, and the screens are notified. The calendar screen listens for this: after a reservation, it reloads itself, even if hidden behind the reservation window;
    • line 44: when the user changes, everything is cleared without notifying anyone: the previous user’s screens will disappear; they have nothing to reload.

    // =========================================================================
// lib/formatage.dart - display of hours and days
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The server sends data BRUTES (start_hour: 8, start_minute: 0; day:
// "2026-10-05"); the formatting, which depends on the language, is the responsibility
// the client (see example 09).
// =========================================================================

import 'package:intl/intl.dart';

import 'api/types.dart';

String _deux(int n) => n.toString().padLeft(2, '0');

// "8:05" rather than "8:5"
String heure(int h, int m) => '$h:${_deux(m)}';

// "8:00 - 8:20"
String horaire(Creneau c) => '${heure(c.hdebut, c.mdebut)} - ${heure(c.hfin, c.mfin)}';

// a date -> "yyyy-MM-dd" (the format of API)
String versJour(DateTime d) => '${d.year}-${_deux(d.month)}-${_deux(d.day)}';

String aujourdhui() => versJour(DateTime.now());

// true if "day" is a valid date in the yyyy-MM-dd format
bool estUneDateValide(String jour) {
  if (!RegExp(r'^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$').hasMatch(jour)) return false;
  final d = DateTime.tryParse(jour);
  return d != null && versJour(d) == jour; // 2026-02-30 -> 2026-03-02: rejected
}

// "Monday, October 5, 2026"
String jourLong(String jour, String langue) => DateFormat.yMMMMEEEEd(langue).format(DateTime.parse(jour));

    Formatting the raw data from the server (see example 09):

    • line 22: a [DateTime] in the format of API (“2026-10-05”);
    • lines 27–30: Is the date in the address valid? [DateTime.tryParse] accepts “2026-02-30” (March 2): we verify that the same string is present;
    • line 34: “Monday, October 5, 2026” or “lundi 5 octobre 2026,” depending on the language ([DateFormat.yMMMMEEEEd] derived from [intl]).

    // =========================================================================
// lib/routeur.dart - application screens and their access permissions
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The MÊMES URLs that other clients use (/login, /calendar, /doctors,
// /my-space...). On the web, they appear in the address bar;
// on a phone, they remain invisible but still organize
// the app (and the stack of screens for the Back button).
//
// All screens are in a ShellRoute, including the widget, Template, and the
// appears between the top bar and the error area.
//
// The GARDES: the redirect function of the GoRouter is called before CHAQUE
// navigation. It can be asynchronous: the first time (when
// the application, F5 on the web), it waits for the server’s response to the
// question “Who is logged in?” (session.verifier()). Then it checks the
// permissions for the requested screen (droitsDe), and redirects if necessary.
// RAPPEL: These checks are merely a CONFORT (do not display an
// is unnecessary). Data protection is ensured by the server, which
// verifies the token and role for each CHAQUE request.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';

import 'api/rdvmedecins_api.dart';
import 'api/types.dart';
import 'etat/messages.dart';
import 'etat/session.dart';
import 'pages/agenda.dart';
import 'pages/connexion.dart';
import 'pages/espace_patient.dart';
import 'pages/inscription.dart';
import 'pages/mon_compte.dart';
import 'pages/page_erreur.dart';
import 'pages/personne_formulaire.dart';
import 'pages/personnes.dart';
import 'widgets/gabarit.dart';

// the access rights for a screen: public (without login), or restricted to
// certain roles (null: all logged-in roles)
typedef Droits = ({bool public, Set<Role>? roles});

Droits droitsDe(String chemin) => switch (chemin) {
   '/login' || '/registration' => (public: true, roles: null),
  _ when chemin.startsWith('/medecins') || chemin.startsWith('/clients') => (public: false, roles: {Role.admin}),
   '/my-space' || '/my-account' => (public: false, roles: {Role.user}),
   '/calendar' || '/restricted' || '/' => (public: false, roles: null),
  _ => (public: true, roles: null), // unknown address: 404 page for all
};

// only one path: INTERNE ("/doctors"): never "//autre-site.com"
String? cheminInterne(String? r) => r != null && r.startsWith('/') && !r.startsWith('//') ? r: null;

// "3" -> 3; "", "abc", "-2", missing (null) -> null
int? entierPositif(String? valeur) {
  final n = int.tryParse(valeur ?? '');
  return n != null && n > 0 ? n : null;
}

GoRouter creerRouteur(Session session, Messages messages, RdvMedecinsApi api) {
   // the three screens for managing doctors OU for clients (ADMIN)
  List<GoRoute> routesPersonnes(TypePersonnes type) => [
    GoRoute(
      path: '/${type.name}',
      builder: (_, _) => PagePersonnes(type: type),
    ),
    GoRoute(
      path: '/${type.name}/ajouter',
      builder: (_, _) => PagePersonneFormulaire(type: type),
    ),
    GoRoute(
      path: '/${type.name}/:id/modifier',
      builder: (_, etat) {
        final id = entierPositif(etat.pathParameters['id']);
         // /doctors/abc/edit: this address does not exist
        return id == null ? const PageErreur(code: 404) : PagePersonneFormulaire(type: type, id: id);
      },
    ),
  ];

  return GoRouter(
    initialLocation: '/login',
     // Session changes (login, logout, expiration): the on-call schedules
     // are recalculated for the current screen
    refreshListenable: session,
    redirect: (context, etat) async {
      await session.verifier();
      final utilisateur = session.utilisateur;
      final chemin = etat.uri.path;
      final droits = droitsDe(chemin);
      if (droits.public) {
         // logged in: the login screen is no longer relevant. It is ICI that
         // exits, immediately after logging in: the session has changed, and the router
         // (which is listening for it) reevaluates its watchers. We go to the requested screen before
         // the connection (?redirect=...), otherwise to the role’s home page
        if (chemin == '/login' && utilisateur != null) {
          return cheminInterne(etat.uri.queryParameters['redirect']) ?? utilisateur.pageAccueil;
        }
        return null;
      }
      if (utilisateur == null) {
         // intentional logout: simply the login screen
        if (session.departVolontaire) return '/login';
         // session expired, page opened without being logged in: we save
         // the requested screen, to return to it after logging in
        return Uri(path: '/login', queryParameters: {'redirect': etat.uri.toString()}).toString();
      }
      if (chemin == '/') return utilisateur.pageAccueil;
      if (droits.roles != null && !droits.roles!.contains(utilisateur.role)) return '/interdit';
      return null;
    },
    routes: [
      ShellRoute(
        builder: (context, etat, child) => Gabarit(child: child),
        routes: [
          GoRoute(path: '/', builder: (_, _) => const PageErreur(code: 404)), // (redirected above)
          GoRoute(
            path: '/login',
            builder: (_, etat) {
               // the login for the URL: 30 characters maximum
              final login = etat.uri.queryParameters['login'] ?? '';
              return PageConnexion(login: login.length > 30 ? login.substring(0, 30) : login);
            },
          ),
          GoRoute(
            path: '/agenda',
            builder: (_, etat) => PageAgenda(
              idMedecin: entierPositif(etat.uri.queryParameters['idMedecin']),
              jour: etat.uri.queryParameters['jour'],
              reserver: entierPositif(etat.uri.queryParameters['reserver']),
            ),
          ),
          ...routesPersonnes(TypePersonnes.medecins),
          ...routesPersonnes(TypePersonnes.clients),
          GoRoute(
            path: '/inscription',
             // a guard PROPRE on this route: no passcode (captcha
             // resolved on the login screen), return to the login screen
            redirect: (context, etat) async {
              final valide = await api.etatAccesInscription().catchError((_) => false);
              if (valide) return null;
              messages.flash(succes: false, cle: 'ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT');
              return '/login';
            },
            builder: (_, _) => const PageInscription(),
          ),
          GoRoute(path: '/mon-espace', builder: (_, _) => const PageEspacePatient()),
          GoRoute(path: '/mon-compte', builder: (_, _) => const PageMonCompte()),
          GoRoute(path: '/interdit', builder: (_, _) => const PageErreur(code: 403)),
        ],
      ),
    ],
     // an address not recognized by any route: 404 page, in the template
    errorBuilder: (context, etat) => const Gabarit(child: PageErreur(code: 404)),
  );
}

    The application screens, their addresses, and their access rights (see examples 17 and 18).

    • Line 40: a screen’s access rights: public, or restricted to certain roles ([null]: all roles);
    • Lines 42–47: the permissions for each address; in UN, only one location: a [switch] string expression. ['/login' || '/inscription']: an “or” pattern; [_ when ...]: an “anything” pattern, with a condition (a guard);
    • line 51: the address [?redirect=] is only followed if it is a path INTERNE: on the web, an address [/login?redirect=//site-pirate.com] sent by email must not take the user elsewhere after they log in;
    • lines 54–56: The parameters of an address are strings, written by anyone (on the web): “abc” or “-2” become [null];
    • lines 61–78: a local function that generates the three routes for the doctors’ OU from the clients: [/medecins], [/medecins/ajouter], [/medecins/:id/modifier]. [:id]: a path parameter, read by [etat.pathParameters['id']];
    • line 81: the initial screen on the phone (on the web, this is the address entered);
    • line 84: the router monitors the session: with each change (connection, disconnection, expiration), it reevaluates its guards for the current screen and switches screens if necessary;
    • lines 85–109: LE guard, called before each navigation:
      • line 86: the first time, we wait for the server’s response to the question “who is logged in?”; after that, this call costs nothing;
      • lines 90–98: A public screen is accessible to everyone; however, a logged-in user has no business being on the login screen: they go to the screen they requested before logging in, or to the home screen for their role. This is how the application exits the login screen after a successful login: the login screen itself does not need to navigate;
      • lines 100–105: No one is logged in: proceed to the login screen. After a session has expired, or if a protected URL (on the web) was opened directly, the requested screen ([?redirect=]) is retained so that the user can return to it after logging in; after an intentional logout, it is not retained;
      • lines 107–108: [/] leads to the role’s home page; an insufficient role leads to a 403 page;
    • lines 112–113: All screens are displayed within the template (the top bar, the menu, the messages);
    • lines 117–121: [/login?login=jbernard] (after creating an account) pre-fills the login field;
    • lines 125–129: the three calendar parameters, read from the URL; the entire screen state is present there (see [agenda.dart]);
    • lines 135–142: a PROPRE token for a route: account creation requires a pass, which the server issues once the CAPTCHA has been entered ([POST /api/inscription/acces], see login screen). Without it, you are redirected to the login screen with a message;
    • line 153: an address not mapped to any route: the 404 page, as defined in the template.

    These safeguards are merely a formality: they prevent a useless screen from being displayed. Data protection is ensured by the server, which re-verifies the token and role with every request.

    // =========================================================================
// lib/widgets/gabarit.dart - the GABARIT common to all screens
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The router’s ShellRoute widget (see routeur.dart):
//    - the top bar: title, language (FR / EN), logout;
//    - the side menu (“drawer”), opened by the ☰ button: the
//      screens permitted for the user’s role. “Doctors” and “Clients”
//      appear only for the ADMIN: this is simply for display convenience; the
//      actual protection is provided by the server;
//    - a success message in HAUT;
//    - the current screen (child);
//    - the error area in BAS.
// On a large screen (web, tablet), the menu is displayed permanently
// on the left: a NavigationRail instead of the drawer.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';

import '../etat/messages.dart';
import '../etat/session.dart';
import '../i18n/traductions.dart';

// A menu entry: path, label key, icon
typedef EntreeMenu = ({String chemin, String cle, IconData icone});

List<EntreeMenu> entreesMenu(Session session) {
  final u = session.utilisateur;
  if (u == null) return const [];
  return [
    if (u.estPatient) (chemin: '/mon-espace', cle: 'APP.MENU_MY_SPACE', icone: Icons.home),
    (chemin: '/agenda', cle: 'APP.MENU_AGENDA', icone: Icons.calendar_month),
    if (u.estAdmin) ...[
      (chemin: '/medecins', cle: 'APP.MENU_DOCTORS', icone: Icons.medical_services),
      (chemin: '/clients', cle: 'APP.MENU_PATIENTS', icone: Icons.people),
    ],
    if (u.estPatient) (chemin: '/mon-compte', cle: 'APP.MENU_ACCOUNT', icone: Icons.manage_accounts),
  ];
}

class Gabarit extends StatelessWidget {
  final Widget child;

  const Gabarit({super.key, required this.child});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final traductions = context.watch<Traductions>();
    final t = traductions.t;
    final session = context.watch<Session>();
    final u = session.utilisateur;
    final entrees = entreesMenu(session);
     // the current address, as known to the router
    final chemin = GoRouter.of(context).routerDelegate.currentConfiguration.uri.path;
    final actif = entrees.indexWhere((e) => chemin.startsWith(e.chemin));
     // MediaQuery: screen dimensions; if greater than 800 points, a large screen
    final grandEcran = MediaQuery.sizeOf(context).width >= 800;

     // the session times out; the router, which is listening for it, displays the login screen
    Future<void> seDeconnecter() => session.deconnecter().catchError((_) {}); // even if the server does not respond

    final contenu = Column(
      crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.stretch,
      children: [
        const _MessageSucces(),
        Expanded(child: child),
        const _ZoneErreur(),
      ],
    );

    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(
        title: Text(t('APP.TITLE')),
        backgroundColor: Theme.of(context).colorScheme.primary,
        foregroundColor: Theme.of(context).colorScheme.onPrimary,
        actions: [
           // FR / EN: no request is sent to the server; the screen is rendered locally
          PopupMenuButton<String>(
            tooltip: t('APP.LANGUAGE'),
             // text, in the color of the toolbar icons (onPrimary)
            icon: Text(
              traductions.langue.toUpperCase(),
              style: TextStyle(fontWeight: FontWeight.bold, color: Theme.of(context).colorScheme.onPrimary),
            ),
            onSelected: traductions.changerLangue,
            itemBuilder: (_) => [for (final l in langues) PopupMenuItem(value: l, child: Text(l.toUpperCase()))],
          ),
          if (u != null) IconButton(tooltip: t('APP.LOGOUT'), icon: const Icon(Icons.logout), onPressed: seDeconnecter),
        ],
      ),
       // the drawer: only when logged in, and only on a small screen
      drawer: u == null || grandEcran
          ? null
          : NavigationDrawer(
              selectedIndex: actif < 0 ? null : actif,
              onDestinationSelected: (i) {
                Navigator.pop(context); // closes the drawer
                context.go(entrees[i].chemin);
              },
              children: [
                 // Header: Who is logged in
                Padding(
                  padding: const EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(28, 16, 16, 10),
                  child: Column(
                    crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
                    children: [
                      Text(u.nom, style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleMedium),
                      Chip(label: Text(u.role.name.toUpperCase())),
                    ],
                  ),
                ),
                for (final e in entrees) NavigationDrawerDestination(icon: Icon(e.icone), label: Text(t(e.cle))),
              ],
            ),
      body: u == null || !grandEcran
          ? contenu
          : Row(
              children: [
                NavigationRail(
                  selectedIndex: actif < 0 ? null : actif,
                  labelType: NavigationRailLabelType.all,
                  onDestinationSelected: (i) => context.go(entrees[i].chemin),
                  destinations: [
                    for (final e in entrees) NavigationRailDestination(icon: Icon(e.icone), label: Text(t(e.cle))),
                  ],
                ),
                const VerticalDivider(width: 1),
                Expanded(child: contenu),
              ],
            ),
    );
  }
}

// the success message, at the top
class _MessageSucces extends StatelessWidget {
  const _MessageSucces();

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final succes = context.watch<Messages>().succes;
    if (succes == null) return const SizedBox.shrink();
    final t = context.watch<Traductions>().t;
    return Material(
      color: Colors.green.shade50,
      child: ListTile(
        leading: Icon(Icons.check_circle, color: Colors.green.shade700),
        title: Text(t(succes.cle, succes.params), style: TextStyle(color: Colors.green.shade900)),
        trailing: IconButton(icon: const Icon(Icons.close), onPressed: context.read<Messages>().effacer),
      ),
    );
  }
}

// the error area, at the bottom: always visible, even when scrolling
class _ZoneErreur extends StatelessWidget {
  const _ZoneErreur();

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final erreur = context.watch<Messages>().erreur;
    if (erreur == null) return const SizedBox.shrink();
    final t = context.watch<Traductions>().t;
    return Material(
      color: const Color(0xFFF8D7DA),
       // SafeArea: above the phone's navigation bar
      child: SafeArea(
        top: false,
        child: ListTile(
          leading: Icon(Icons.error, color: Colors.red.shade800),
          title: Text(t(erreur.cle, erreur.params), style: TextStyle(color: Colors.red.shade900)),
          trailing: IconButton(icon: const Icon(Icons.close), onPressed: context.read<Messages>().effacer),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}

    The [ShellRoute] widget: the element that surrounds all screens.

    • Line 26: a menu entry: a record;
    • lines 28–38: entries permitted for the user’s role, via a [if] in a list (example 03). [...[...]]: the decomposition operator inserts multiple elements at once;
    • line 55: the current address, to mark the active menu entry;
    • line 58: the screen width, in points. Above 800 points (the web, a tablet in landscape mode), the menu will be displayed permanently;
    • line 61: logout—the session is cleared, and the router, which is listening for this, displays the login screen. [catchError]: even if the server does not respond, the user is considered logged out;
    • lines 63–68: the success message at the top, the screen in the middle ([Expanded]: all remaining space), the error at the bottom;
    • lines 73–89: the top bar: the title, the language menu ([PopupMenuButton]: a button that opens a list; its icon here is text, “FR” or “EN”), the logout button;
    • lines 93–113: on a small screen, a drawer ([NavigationDrawer]), which opens via the ☰ button that [Scaffold] automatically adds to the top bar. Tapping an entry closes the drawer ([Navigator.pop]) and changes the URL;
    • Lines 116–129: On a large screen, a [NavigationRail]: the menu, arranged in a column to the left of the content;
    • lines 137–154: the success message. [context.watch<Messages>()]: the widget is rebuilt every time the messages change; when there are no messages, it takes up no space ([SizedBox.shrink]);
    • lines 168–169: the error area is at the bottom of the screen: [SafeArea] keeps it separate from the phone’s navigation bar (the buttons or gesture bar of [Android]).

    // =========================================================================
// lib/widgets/envoi_formulaire.dart - send a form to the server
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// All forms in the app follow the same pattern as
// Example 25: no rules are checked on the phone (they reside
// in a single location—the server—and in case of rejection:
//    - the error for each field (ErreurApi.champs) is displayed below the field;
//    - the general message (ErreurApi.cle) appears at the bottom of the screen.
// This class groups these actions (it is the Command from Example 23,
// supplemented with field errors). A screen creates one per form:
//
//      final _envoi = EnvoiFormulaire(messages);
//      if (await _envoi.envoyer(() => api.inscrire(input))) { ... }
//      ChampSaisie(..., error: _submit.errors['nom'])
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';

import '../api/erreur_api.dart';
import '../etat/messages.dart';

class EnvoiFormulaire extends ChangeNotifier {
  final Messages _messages;
   // the error for each field: a CLÉ translation
  Map<String, String> erreurs = {};
   // error message parameters ({{min}}...), returned by the server
  Map<String, String> params = {};
  bool enCours = false;

  EnvoiFormulaire(this._messages);

   // executes the send; returns true if successful. In case of ErreurApi, the
   // errors are displayed and false is returned
  Future<bool> envoyer(Future<void> Function() action) async {
    if (enCours) return false; // no duplicate submission
    erreurs = {};
    params = {};
    enCours = true;
    notifyListeners();
    try {
      await action();
      return true;
    } on ErreurApi catch (e) {
      _messages.afficherErreurApi(e);
      erreurs = e.champs;
      params = e.params;
      return false;
    } finally {
      enCours = false;
      notifyListeners();
    }
  }

   // the user modifies a field: the error disappears
  void effacerErreur(String champ) {
    if (erreurs.containsKey(champ)) {
      erreurs = {...erreurs}..remove(champ);
      notifyListeners();
    }
  }
}

    Submitting a form to the server: the [Commande] from Example 23, supplemented with field errors (Example 25).

    • Lines 34–50: Submission: no duplicate submissions; during submission, [enCours] (the buttons are disabled); if [ErreurApi] occurs, the general message at the bottom of the screen and the error for each field are displayed. [finally] runs in all cases, even after a [return];
    • lines 55–57: the user corrects a field; the error disappears. We replace the [Map] with a copy, rather than modifying it: the old one may have been provided by the server ([e.champs]), and a constant [Map] ([const {}]) does not change.
